Visitors can birdwatch and take photographs as they enjoy a wide range of year-round outdoor recreation opportunities and experiences. Ample open space is available for yard games. A multi-use loop trail and nature trails weave through clearings and tree canopy, perfect for quiet dreaming and restful solitude for every season.

Begins at Blanchard River Nature Preserve (22006 CR 17, Forest — COUNTY_VERIFY: may be Hardin County), ends at Blanchard Landing (SR 235 S of US 224 W, Findlay — Hancock). If start is in Hardin County, CROSS_COUNTY_CANDIDATE for Hancock + Hardin. Access points: Blanchard River NP (start), Jackson Landing, Riverbend Recreation Area (primitive campground), Waterfalls Area (portage), Great Karg Well (portage), Liberty Landing (9.3mi float start), Blanchard Landing (end). Downstream of Blanchard Landing continues to Putnam County (not part of designated BRWT).

trails.name: Blanchard River Greenway Trail
trails.identity_notes: Urban greenway linking parks and downtown Findlay. Route: Bright Road (eastern terminus at Eastpoint Area) to Fox Street (western terminus at River Landings), with connection to Broad Avenue and Township Road 89. Passes through seven River Parks: Eastpoint Area, Waterfalls Area, Riverside Park Waterfront (T6 — City of Findlay), Centennial Park, Great Karg Well Historical Site, River Landings, and HPD Administrative Offices. Riverside Park Waterfront is no longer HPD-managed (agreement ended Jan 1 2026) — will be T6 entity.

trails.name: Findlay Reservoir Dike Trail
trails.governance: City of Findlay — Water Department; Ohio Department of Natural Resources Division of Wildlife (cooperative management)
trails.identity_notes: T6 MISS — found during T8 discovery pass 2026-05-15. Earthen dike trail surrounding Findlay Reservoirs #1 and #2 (City of Findlay municipal water supply). Reservoir #1 dike = 2.0 miles; Reservoir #2 dike = 4.3 miles; shared dike between reservoirs = 1.0 mile; outer perimeter of combined reservoir system = 5.3 miles (source: hiking-ohio.com). Trail on City of Findlay earthen infrastructure dikes; ODNR cooperative agreement covers recreation access. Notable as eBird hotspot L285907 (Findlay Reservoirs) — popular winter waterfowl birding. Often described in conjunction with Riverbend Recreation Area (HPD T3) — physically adjacent but distinct governance. Staged at discovery_tier=6 (City of Findlay). GPS pending GPS Acquisition Module pass. Seeded from Copilot baseline (Findlay Reservoir Trail).
